Package com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest

Class HmacAuthenticator

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest.HmacAuthenticator
public final class HmacAuthenticator extends Object
Generic HMAC request signer for the many bespoke "sign a canonical string with a shared secret" auth schemes that APIs roll themselves (as opposed to the fully-specified AWS SigV4). Pure and side-effect-free: it builds a string-to-sign from a caller-supplied template, HMACs it with the secret, and returns the header(s) to add. The HMAC chain is verified offline against the RFC 4231 known-answer vectors (see HmacAuthenticatorTest).

Both the string-to-sign and the header-value are templates over a small placeholder set, so a user can express most real schemes without code:

  • {method} — upper-cased HTTP method
  • {path} — request path (leading /)
  • {query} — raw query string ("" when none)
  • {url} — the full request URI
  • {host} — host[:port]
  • {date} — current time as an RFC 1123 GMT date (also emitted as a Date header so the server can reconstruct the same string)
  • {body} — request body as UTF-8 text
  • {body-sha256-hex} / {body-sha256-base64} — digest of the body
  • {keyId} — the (non-secret) key/access id
  • {signature} — the computed signature (header-value template only)
Use a literal \n in a template to embed a newline (the typical line-oriented canonical form, e.g. {method}\n{path}\n{date}).

      Computes the HMAC auth header(s) for a request.
      Returns:
      an ordered map of header name → value to add to the outgoing request. Always contains headerName; additionally contains Date when the string-to-sign uses {date} (so the value is verifiable server-side).
